condition.expression: switching_present AND fb_present AND rail_voltage_present AND NOT pgood_measured

next_steps.action: Measure the controller's PGOOD pin. PGOOD is open-drain with an external pull-up; the pin voltage is high when the controller declares the rail good.

measure.where: Controller PGOOD pin (consult datasheet) and the PGOOD pull-up resistor
measure.instrument: DMM DC volts + oscilloscope to check for chatter
measure.expected: High (= pull-up rail, typically 3.3 V) when rail is good. Low when faulted.
measure.safety: PGOOD is open-drain; if the pin is low the controller is actively pulling it. Do NOT assume the pin is dead just because it is low.

interpretations.then: Rail is good. If the system still does not progress, the issue is downstream of this rail (sequencing, next rail, or load).

interpretations.if_result: PGOOD low while rail voltage is correct
interpretations.then: Controller is not declaring PGOOD despite good output. Possible causes: PGOOD pull-up rail missing, PGOOD comparator threshold mismatch, or controller internal fault. Check the PGOOD pull-up source first.
Rail is on the edge of regulation. Check ripple, load transients, and the FB divider. Output capacitors degraded?

next_steps.requires_info_note: Need controller datasheet for PGOOD pin and PGOOD assertion conditions.
